gold_steps_without_duration_evidence.activity_name: Obtain the water-flow letter and hydrant map from the water company
Sequence the concurrent building and fire reviews and set their per-discipline due dates
Field inspections against the ADU Inspection Checklist (Bulletin 213)
Review and preapprove a vendor's standard ADU plans (a separate vendor-facing pipeline)
Wait on interdepartmental dependencies with no systematic tracking
Issue specific and comprehensive Plan Check Comments telling the applicant exactly what must change
Obtain the written approvals that gate issuance (well & septic, health officer, zoning, grading, stormwater, fire, encroachment, water/sewer clearance)
Pay a published private firm for third-party plan check on an expedited basis
Field inspections at foundation pouring, framing, electrical installation and final completion
Halt the project and require corrections when non-compliance is found at inspection

coverage.notes: adu_permit's underlying corpus is genuinely thin on measured cycle times: both gold models state outright that no end-to-end duration distribution exists for ADU permitting at any of the three implementer cities (San José, Sonoma County, Oakland, Berkeley, Sacramento all appear only via targets, statutory ceilings, or n=1 community reports). Field inspection (task_type=inspection) has ZERO duration evidence at any tier across both gold models and the entire reddit/sources corpus for this slug — the single largest structural gap. A fresh keyword sweep of all 135 reddit posts not already curated into sources.json (170 total minus 35 curated) found no additional on-topic duration statements beyond noise/contamination, consistent with the corpus's own recon notes.

observations.jurisdiction: State of California (statewide statutory clock, Gov. Code § 66317)
observations.step_label: ADU completeness determination (statewide statutory clock)
observations.quote: provide written notice of this determination to the applicant not later than 15 business days after the permitting agency received the application.
observations.notes: Ceiling, not a measurement. Applies to every CA permitting agency reviewing an ADU application; San José's own process page never mentions it (a known availability gap per the gold model).

observations.jurisdiction: State of California (statewide statutory clock, Gov. Code § 66317)
observations.step_label: Deemed-complete backstop if the 15-business-day completeness clock is missed
observations.quote: If a permitting agency does not make a timely determination as required by this paragraph, the application or resubmitted application shall be deemed to be complete for the purposes of this section.
observations.notes: Same 15-business-day figure as the prior observation, framed as the backstop rather than the primary clock. Recorded separately because it is a distinct process step (a notice/consequence, not the review itself).

observations.jurisdiction: State of California (statewide statutory clock, Gov. Code § 66317)
observations.step_label: ADU ministerial approve/deny (statewide statutory clock)
observations.quote: The permitting agency shall either approve or deny the application to create or serve an accessory dwelling unit within 60 days from the date the permitting agency receives a completed application.
observations.notes: 60 CALENDAR days (not business days) — distinct from Sonoma's AB 2234 60-BUSINESS-day backstop for large projects; the two clock sets must not be conflated (per the Sonoma gold's own scope_boundary warning). Clock tolls if the applicant requests a delay.

observations.jurisdiction: State of California (statewide statutory clock, Gov. Code § 66317)
observations.step_label: Deemed-approved backstop if the 60-day ministerial clock is missed
observations.quote: If the local agency has not approved or denied the completed application within 60 days, the application shall be deemed approved.
observations.notes: Independently corroborated by a California resident's own accurate lay restatement of this clock (R24, 2026-07-25): "Cities must approve or deny in 60 days, no hearings, checklist review only" — community-side confirmation that the ceiling is understood, not a personal delay experience.

observations.jurisdiction: State of California (statewide statutory clock, Gov. Code § 66317)
observations.step_label: Appeal of a denial or incompleteness determination to the governing body/planning commission
observations.quote: A permitting agency on the appeal shall provide a final written determination by not later than 60 business days after receipt of the applicant's written appeal.
observations.notes: No source in this corpus reports an actual appeal being filed or its real elapsed time for any of the three implementer cities.

observations.step_label: Preapproved-ADU same-day permit issuance at the scheduled plan review meeting
observations.quote: If the site-specific plan and related documents are accurate and complete, permits may be issued on the same day of the scheduled plan review meeting.
observations.notes: A declared capability, not a measured outcome — San José publishes no share of preapproved projects that actually achieve same-day issuance. Excludes projects with a deferred site-specific structural submittal, which 'may take longer.'

observations.quote: New single-family residence | 20 | 10 | 10 | 5 | 10 | 5
observations.notes: NOT ADU-specific. San José's table explicitly excludes the ADU Service appointment track and has no ADU row; used here only as the nearest analogue category, working days (excludes weekends/holidays).

observations.step_label: Permit Intake completeness review (AB 2234 general post-entitlement clock, not ADU-specific)
observations.quote: permit agencies are required to review a permit application for completeness within 15 business days and completed applications must then be assessed for code and ordinance compliance within 30 business days.
observations.notes: AB 2234 (Gov. Code §65913.3) is Sonoma's GENERAL post-entitlement clock, not ADU-specific; it runs alongside and is shorter than Gov. Code §66317's ADU-specific 15-business-day/60-calendar-day clocks (see state-level observations). D1 (grand jury) quotes the bill; the bill text itself (D4) was not held by this recon.

observations.step_label: Resubmittal after an incompleteness notice resets the 15-business-day completeness clock
observations.quote: AB 2234 makes it clear that if an applicant is informed that documentation is incomplete or inadequate, the 15-day clock resets.
observations.notes: Each cure-and-resubmit cycle restarts the 15-day clock from zero; no cap on the number of cycles is stated.

observations.step_label: Multi-division plan check after plan-check-fee payment (AB 2234, <25 housing units)
observations.quote: Payment of this plan check fee triggers a second clock under AB 2234: review the plans and issue the permit within 30 business days or tell the applicant why it isn't acceptable.
observations.notes: The single most consequential designed detail in this model: the clock starts on FEE PAYMENT, not on submittal or acceptance — an applicant who delays payment delays their own statutory protection. Nothing in the statute states this; it is a Sonoma administrative design choice.

observations.step_label: Deemed-approved/considered-accepted backstop if Permit Sonoma misses the AB 2234 review deadline
observations.quote: If a local agency does not adhere to the 30- or 60- business day limit for reviewing applications, the application is deemed approved under certain conditions.
observations.notes: 30 business days for projects under 25 housing units (the ADU case); 60 business days for 25 or more. No Sonoma applicant-facing document was fetched confirming whether Permit Sonoma discloses this right to applicants.

observations.step_label: Actual staff working time on a residential plan check (touch time only)
observations.quote: a typical residential construction plan check takes 4-8 hours of staff time
observations.notes: TOUCH time only (4-8 hours ≈ 0.5-1 working day), anecdotal — 'Accela does not capture real processing times' so this is interview-derived, not measured. Pairs with the elapsed-time observation below as this corpus's clearest touch-vs-queue illustration.

observations.step_label: Elapsed time for the same plan check to work through the system (queue-dominated)
observations.quote: If a permit plan check takes 4-8-12 hours, why does it take 4-8-12 weeks to work its way through the system?
observations.notes: 4-8-12 weeks = 28-84 days elapsed vs. 4-8 hours (~0.5-1 day) of touch time — nearly all of the gap is queue_days, but no queue-only figure is separately published; this is the grand jury's own rhetorical framing of the gap, not a statistical distribution (n=1 characterisation, not a sampled median).

observations.step_label: Building Permit average days to review (June 2023 baseline, agency self-report)
observations.quote: In aggregate, the result is a 57% reduction in processing times across the department's most common permit types without compromising critical compliance reviews that keep our community safe.
observations.notes: Value comes from D1's reconstruction of a Feb-2024 Board-update table (not itself a verbatim quote); 68% reduction claimed; December-2024 value lost to OCR. Treat as an agency self-report, unaudited — D1's Finding F4 disputes reliability, and two different aggregate reduction figures (57% vs 67%) appear in adjacent quotations of the same underlying document. observations.step_label: Measured compliance with the 15-business-day completeness deadline (grand jury record review)
observations.quote: failed to review applications for completeness and acceptability within the 15-day limit a handful of times - out of more than 7,000 permit applications
observations.notes: A compliance RATE against the ceiling, not a duration distribution — but genuinely measured (grand jury manual review), unlike the anecdotal touch/elapsed figures above. n=7,000+ 2024 permit applications (all types, not ADU-specific).

observations.step_label: Measured compliance with the 30-business-day plan-check deadline (grand jury record review)
observations.quote: fewer than 20 of ~1,100 permit applications requiring plan check failed to meet the AB 2234 requirements. All of the failures were permits that required review by multiple departments
observations.notes: Manual review of 5,000+ task-status records for February and October 2024. All failures involved multi-department review — corroborates the interdepartmental-coordination gap (A10) as the actual failure driver, not raw workload. n=~1,100 (all permit types, not ADU-specific).

observations.step_label: Express Permit ad hoc cross-division review, fall-2024 first trial
observations.quote: half a dozen permit applications were reviewed and issued in an afternoon, saving weeks of time for applicants with no additional work on Permit Sonoma's part
observations.notes: Self-reported by the Express Permit team, unaudited. One engineer from each plan-check division reviews together and approves on the spot for routine applications.

observations.step_label: Express Permit ad hoc cross-division review, sustained weekly pilot throughput
observations.quote: beyond the 8-10 typically processed during the current pilot
observations.notes: 8-10 permits per weekly session during the pilot (vs. 'half a dozen' at the fall-2024 first trial) — same-session issuance sustained over multiple weeks, illustrating the taxonomy's 'weekly' cadence directly.

observations.step_label: Over-the-counter issuance for minor work with no structural modification (no plan check)
observations.quote: Building permits for minor work, such as a re-roof, new water heater, electric upgrade or other work that does not involve any structural modification, can be issued over the counter.
observations.notes: Bypasses plan check entirely. The eligibility list for this track is itself unpublished (D1 had to reconstruct it from six months of issued permits) — a genuine availability gap distinct from the duration figure itself.

observations.step_label: System-wide average time-in-process, all Permit Sonoma permit types (order-of-magnitude estimate)
observations.quote: At any given time, PS has a thousand or more permits in some stage of completion, is working on 500-1,000 new applications every month
observations.notes: COMPUTED BY US, not stated by D1: Little's Law estimate = WIP ÷ throughput ≈ 1,000 permits ÷ 750/month ≈ 1.3 months ≈ 40 days. Aggregates ALL Permit Sonoma permit types (not ADU-specific), and assumes steady-state arrivals=completions, which D1's own 2024 backlog-reduction narrative suggests was not true during this period — treat as an order-of-magnitude sanity check only, not a citable figure.

observations.jurisdiction: Sacramento, CA area (r/Sacramento; city vs. county not specified by poster)
observations.step_label: Custom-design ADU: builder signing to city plan approval
observations.quote: December–January: Felt like very little progress (this part was frustrating but a lot of back and forth between them and the city plus holiday dead zones)... Mid-February: Plans approved by the city
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; selection-biased toward whatever the poster found noteworthy (here, actually a fairly positive account: 'After approval: Everything moved FAST'). ~3.5 months late-Nov signing to mid-Feb approval; not isolated from design/back-and-forth time.

observations.step_label: Community judgment on the practical impact of the 15-business-day SB 543 completeness clock
observations.quote: The 15 day permitting thing really isn't that big of a deal because most builders need to get all their d[ocuments ready anyway]
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit comment; not a personal delay experience but a real-world judgment that the statutory ceiling rarely binds because applicant-side prep already takes longer.

observations.step_label: Monthly in-person walk-in day for same-day approval of certain ADU plans
observations.quote: At this point you can actually go in one Tuesday a month and get certain plans approved in a single day for an EDU, so it's gone down.
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; selection-biased. Describes an appointment cadence not named in any San José declared-tier source (S6-S9) — a genuine availability gap this quote fills. 'EDU' appears to be the poster's typo/shorthand for ADU.

observations.jurisdiction: unspecified San Francisco Bay Area city, CA (not named by poster; non-ADU permit)
observations.step_label: Room addition permit and approval wait (non-ADU, same-region comparator)
observations.quote: just waiting for the permits and approvals would take around nine months at best
observations.notes: NOT an ADU permit — a general residential room-addition permit in an unnamed Bay Area city. Included only as a same-region queue-time comparator, not scored against the ADU-specific gold process directly. Single self-selected report, selection-biased toward delay.

observations.step_label: Detached ADU permit application to permit issuance
observations.quote: I need a permit, so I need to wait another 6 months
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; selection-biased toward delay. Poster contrasts with their own already-issued attached-ADU permit in the same thread.

observations.jurisdiction: unspecified California city (not named by poster)
observations.step_label: Overall ADU project, city side of permitting/inspection described as slow
observations.quote: the city has been absolutely useless and extremely slow in the permitting/inspection process. Spent endless hours on the phone with city workers who are completely clueless and always give the go around.
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; strong selection bias toward dissatisfaction. Jurisdiction not confirmed; ~6 months is the poster's own framing of the overall (design+permit+inspection) timeline, not isolated agency review time.

observations.jurisdiction: unincorporated San Lorenzo, Alameda County, CA (Ora Loma Sanitary District)
observations.step_label: Sanitary-district sewage-plan sign-off, running independently of the county building permit
observations.quote: Started the process of getting a permit for our sewage plan way back in February but jeez has it been an absolute hassle to get anything back... It's been about a month since my last correspondence with them.
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report, ongoing/unresolved at time of posting (180 days is a lower bound: February to the August-25 post date). queue_days=30 is time since the applicant's last correspondence. The applicant's county building-permit structural review had already cleared — only this special-district sign-off, on its own independent clock, was stuck.

observations.step_label: NEW-construction garage-conversion ADU: application to permit issuance
observations.quote: I also managed the process and our permit took 18 months to come through due to the application going in to a blackhole at every step of the process.
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; the single longest user-reported ADU permit-issuance time in this corpus. Explicitly distinguished by the recon from the SAME thread's OP amnesty/legalization timeline (~2 years), which is out of scope for this slug and excluded. Oakland new-construction ADUs over $100k also require a separate EBMUD sewer-lateral certification (no duration stated for that sub-step specifically).

observations.step_label: Garage-to-ADU conversion on a lot-line structure, still pending
observations.quote: Trying to convert to an ADU, Oakland wants a Survey and it is not cheap at all. Been a year since trying to get permit.
observations.notes: Single self-selected reddit report; still pending/unresolved at post date, so 365 days is a lower bound, not a completed elapsed time. Selection-biased toward delay.

observations.jurisdiction: unspecified California (poster does not name a city; total project incl. delivery/construction)
observations.step_label: Prefab ADU delivery: full project completion
observations.quote: Going the prefab route... will be the smoothest, and least expensive... Building on site, or using “pre-approved plans” will be more expensive, more variables and will take longer to get through the permitting process.
observations.notes: Heavily caveated: this is a TOTAL project timeline (design + factory build + delivery + final on-site permitting), not an isolated plan-review or inspection duration — factory units are pre-inspected before shipping, leaving only prep/final attachment for the city to review on site. No comparable number given for the slower site-built/pre-approved-plan alternative. agency_class set to null: this figure spans multiple actors (factory build, delivery, city plan review/inspection) with no single agency_class applicable.
